purpose: machine-facing knowledge searcher node for finding, retrieving, evaluating, and synthesizing authoritative knowledge organization work units across classification scheme design, indexing language construction, indexing policy, automation, quality evaluation, and governance
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all metrics are heuristic priors
subdomain of information science & knowledge organization
nodes are session-bounded, evaluable work units of classification & indexing
general full-text ranking algorithm internals are out of scope except where they consume index design

glossary.definition: scheme that pre-lists all classes including compounds
scheme that composes classmarks from facets via citation order
fixed sequence (e.g., PMEST) in which facets combine into a classmark
symbol system encoding classes and their order/synthesis
notation's capacity to host new subjects without renumbering
managed term set with equivalence/hierarchy/associative relations
justification (literary/user/structural) for including a term or class
number of distinct concepts indexed per document
degree to which an index term precisely names a concept
selecting controlled terms/classes to describe a document
extracting index terms directly from document text
degree two indexers assign the same terms to the same document

evidence_label_policy.rule: no observed/experimentally_validated labels without eligible data; observed_impact/data_quality/observed_co_occurrence=0.0; posterior=normalize(PI*EC)

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for classification & indexing work units, metrics, and relations
grounding_limits: estimates are model heuristics not measurements

nodes.definition: Fix what counts as a classification/indexing work unit, the document/concept universe, and out-of-scope retrieval mechanics.

included: unit of analysis (scheme, index record, decision)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when collection purpose or user population materially shifts

pros.claim: prevents scope creep into full-text retrieval
pros.example: deciding a museum object index excludes free-text OCR search

cons.claim: early scope errors propagate to every downstream node
cons.example: mislabeling a thesaurus task as classification forces rework of notation

failure_modes: scope silently expands to general IR
acceptance_tests: scope doc enumerates included/excluded unit types
every later node maps to one in-scope unit

nodes.definition: Choose among DDC, LCC, UDC, Colon/faceted, or a custom scheme given collection, users, and interoperability needs.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when interoperability target or dominant subject domain changes

pros.claim: matching scheme to collection reduces notation strain
pros.example: narrow law library favors LCC K-class over DDC

cons.claim: switching schemes later is near-irreversible at scale
cons.example: reclassifying a million volumes from DDC to LCC

failure_modes: scheme chosen by familiarity not fit
faceted needs forced into enumerative scheme
acceptance_tests: selected scheme covers >=95% of sampled subjects without strain
revisit_triggers: subject spread broadens beyond scheme strength

nodes.definition: Decide structural paradigm: enumerative listing, faceted/analytico-synthetic composition, or hybrid.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when subjects show high compoundness exceeding enumeration capacity

pros.claim: faceted handles compound/novel subjects without table bloat
pros.example: Colon Classification composes 'statistics of education' from facets

cons.claim: faceted raises notation and indexer-training cost
cons.example: constructing PMEST citation order requires trained analysts

acceptance_tests: paradigm decision justified by subject compoundness sample
facet inventory covers sampled compound subjects

nodes.definition: Define facets/categories and fix citation (combination) order for compound subjects (e.g., PMEST).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when citation order produces inconsistent compound classmarks across indexers

pros.claim: fixed citation order yields predictable, collocating classmarks
pros.example: PMEST keeps personality facet first for consistent shelving

cons.claim: wrong citation order scatters related materials
cons.example: placing energy before personality breaks collocation

acceptance_tests: sampled compound subjects classify identically by two indexers

nodes.definition: Design or apply notation: base, hospitality/expansibility, expressiveness, mnemonics, synthesis devices.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when new subjects cannot be accommodated without renumbering (hospitality failure)

pros.claim: expressive, hospitable notation absorbs new topics without renumbering
pros.example: DDC decimal extension inserts new topics between existing classes

cons.claim: over-expressive notation becomes unwieldy and error-prone
cons.example: very long UDC strings raise transcription errors

acceptance_tests: sampled new subjects insert without renumbering
notation length stays within transcription error budget

nodes.definition: Build/select controlled vocabulary: thesaurus, subject headings, taxonomy with USE/UF, BT/NT/RT relations.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when user query logs reveal recurring unmatched/preferred-term gaps

pros.claim: controlled terms collapse synonyms and disambiguate homographs
pros.example: USE 'maize' UF 'corn' unifies postings under one heading

cons.claim: vocabulary maintenance lags fast-moving domains
cons.example: new technology terms missing for years

acceptance_tests: sampled synonym sets map to one preferred term
homograph terms carry disambiguating scope notes

nodes.definition: Justify inclusion of terms/classes via literary, user, and structural warrant rather than ad hoc choice.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when added terms lack documented warrant and bloat the vocabulary

pros.claim: warrant keeps vocabulary grounded in actual literature and use
pros.example: adding a class only when N documents warrant it

cons.claim: strict warrant can lag emerging but unpublished needs
cons.example: user-warranted terms missing because no literature yet

acceptance_tests: each sampled added term cites warrant type + evidence

nodes.definition: Decide policy mix of controlled-vocabulary indexing vs free-text/derived keyword indexing.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when precision/recall logs show free-text noise or controlled-term miss patterns

pros.claim: controlled boosts precision/recall on known concepts; free-text covers novelty
pros.example: controlled heading + free-text fallback for new slang

cons.claim: controlled-only misses unanticipated terms; free-text-only loses precision
cons.example: free-text 'apple' conflates fruit and company

acceptance_tests: policy backed by precision/recall sample on both modes

nodes.definition: Set indexing depth: exhaustivity (how many concepts per doc) and specificity (how precisely each is named).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when recall too low (under-exhaustive) or precision too low (over-exhaustive)

pros.claim: tuned exhaustivity/specificity directly trades recall vs precision
pros.example: indexing 8 concepts per doc raises recall, lowers precision

cons.claim: high exhaustivity raises cost and noise
cons.example: over-indexing buries the primary subject

acceptance_tests: sampled docs meet exhaustivity target +/-1 concept

nodes.definition: Choose indexing method: human/automatic concept assignment from a vocabulary vs derived/extracted terms from text.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when full text becomes available enabling derived methods at scale

pros.claim: assignment gives consistent controlled access; derived scales cheaply
pros.example: assigning MeSH vs extracting title keywords

cons.claim: derived indexing inherits author vocabulary noise
cons.example: extracted terms miss concepts never named in text

failure_modes: derived used where concept never appears verbatim
assignment used where no vocabulary fits
acceptance_tests: sampled docs indexed by chosen method meet recall target
rationale ties method to text availability

nodes.definition: Design automated classification mapping documents to scheme classes via rules or ML, with confidence handling.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when class distribution shifts or new classes appear (concept drift)

pros.claim: automation scales classification to large/streaming corpora
pros.example: auto-routing patents to IPC subclasses

cons.claim: opaque classifiers misassign rare classes and hide errors
cons.example: long-tail classes starved of training data

acceptance_tests: macro-F1 on held-out set meets target per class group
low-confidence items routed to human review

nodes.definition: Apply supervised/zero-shot text categorization to multi-label subject taxonomies distinct from shelf classification.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when taxonomy adds/merges labels requiring retraining or threshold re-tuning

pros.claim: multi-label categorization fits subjects spanning several taxonomy nodes
pros.example: tagging an article with both 'ethics' and 'AI'

cons.claim: per-label thresholds drift and rare labels underperform
cons.example: tail labels never predicted without threshold tuning

acceptance_tests: per-label precision/recall meets target on sample

nodes.definition: Measure and control consistency among indexers (and human vs machine) for the same document.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when measured consistency falls below policy threshold

pros.claim: consistency measurement exposes ambiguous guidelines
pros.example: two indexers agree on 45% of terms -> guideline fix

cons.claim: low consistency degrades retrieval reliability unpredictably
cons.example: same doc found under different headings by chance

acceptance_tests: Hooper/Rolling consistency computed on dual-indexed sample

nodes.definition: Tune index design (depth, vocabulary granularity, entry vocabulary) to target precision/recall tradeoff.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when retrieval evaluation shows precision/recall off target for key query classes

pros.claim: design levers move precision/recall predictably
pros.example: broader entry vocabulary raises recall on novice queries

cons.claim: optimizing one query class can hurt another
cons.example: precision tuning for experts hurts novice recall

failure_modes: one query class optimized at others' expense
acceptance_tests: precision/recall measured against relevance judgments per query class

nodes.definition: Build entry vocabulary, cross-references, and lead-in terms guiding users from their words to preferred terms.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when query logs show users failing to reach preferred terms

pros.claim: entry vocabulary connects user words to controlled terms
pros.example: 'heart attack' -> USE 'myocardial infarction'

cons.claim: stale cross-references mislead users
cons.example: see-reference points to retired heading

acceptance_tests: sampled user queries reach a preferred term via entry vocabulary

nodes.definition: Design hierarchical relationships and collocation so related subjects gather and broaden/narrow navigation works.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when polyhierarchy or miscollocation confuses broaden/narrow navigation

pros.claim: sound hierarchy enables broaden/narrow and collocation
pros.example: NT chain lets users drill from 'mammals' to 'felines'

cons.claim: deep or poly-hierarchy confuses placement and maintenance
cons.example: a term validly under two parents complicates navigation

acceptance_tests: sampled terms place under correct BT/NT
collocation gathers related subjects on sample

nodes.definition: Maintain vocabulary/scheme over time: add/merge/retire terms, version, propagate changes to existing records.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when term changes risk orphaning or mislinking existing index records

pros.claim: controlled change keeps legacy records findable
pros.example: merging two headings with a USE reference preserves access

cons.claim: uncontrolled changes orphan or mislink existing records
cons.example: retiring a heading without reindexing loses its documents

acceptance_tests: sampled changed terms propagate to existing records

nodes.definition: Map/crosswalk between schemes and vocabularies (DDC<->LCC, local<->LCSH) for shared/federated access.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a federation partner or external scheme version changes

pros.claim: crosswalks enable federated search across schemes
pros.example: mapping local subjects to LCSH for union catalog

cons.claim: imperfect mappings silently lose or broaden meaning
cons.example: mapping a specific local term to a broader LCSH heading

failure_modes: mappings asserted as exact when only broad
acceptance_tests: sampled mappings carry correct match type

nodes.definition: Build evaluation harness: gold standard, relevance judgments, consistency/F1/precision-recall measurement, regression.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when metrics, gold standard, or query mix change enough to invalidate the baseline

pros.claim: a harness turns design choices into measurable regressions
pros.example: CI fails if macro-F1 drops below baseline after retraining

cons.claim: a biased gold standard hides systematic errors
cons.example: gold built only from expert queries misses novice failures

nodes.definition: Govern the whole indexing/classification system: policy of record, decision log, human-review gates, change control.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when high-impact or irreversible policy changes are proposed

pros.claim: governance makes irreversible scheme/vocabulary decisions reviewable
pros.example: change-control board approves scheme migration

cons.claim: heavy governance slows responsive maintenance
cons.example: every term edit waiting on a board meeting

acceptance_tests: high-impact decisions carry decision records + review sign-off

edges.why_related: scope fixes the universe scheme selection must cover
edges.example: scope excluding free-text rules out scheme-as-full-text-engine
edges.resolution_rule: scope dominates; re-select scheme if scope changes

edges.why_related: scope defines concept universe the vocabulary must cover
edges.example: scope limits vocabulary to in-scope subjects
edges.resolution_rule: scope dominates; reissue vocabulary if scope changes

edges.why_related: chosen scheme constrains available structural paradigms
edges.example: LCC favors enumerative; Colon mandates faceted
edges.resolution_rule: scheme constraints dominate paradigm choice

edges.why_related: faceted paradigm requires defined facets and citation order
edges.example: choosing faceted obliges a PMEST-style schedule
edges.resolution_rule: if faceted, facet analysis is mandatory before classmarks

edges.why_related: scheme provides or constrains the notation base
edges.example: adopting DDC inherits decimal notation
edges.resolution_rule: prefer scheme-native notation unless custom justified

edges.why_related: paradigm bounds notation synthesis devices needed
edges.example: faceted needs synthetic connectors enumerative omits
edges.resolution_rule: paradigm sets minimum notation synthesis capability

edges.why_related: vocabulary terms require warrant justification
edges.example: each heading justified by literary/user warrant
edges.resolution_rule: warrant gates term inclusion

edges.why_related: a controlled vocabulary must exist before deciding controlled/free mix
edges.example: MeSH existence enables controlled-vs-free policy
edges.resolution_rule: vocabulary precedes policy decision

edges.why_related: indexing-mode policy frames depth (exhaustivity/specificity) decisions
edges.example: controlled policy enables specificity rules per term
edges.resolution_rule: mode policy precedes depth tuning

edges.why_related: controlled/free policy frames assignment vs derivation method
edges.example: controlled policy implies assignment indexing
edges.resolution_rule: policy dominates method selection

edges.why_related: depth guidelines change achievable inter-indexer consistency
edges.example: tight specificity rules raise indexer agreement
edges.resolution_rule: measure consistency after depth guidelines stabilize

edges.why_related: method choice changes consistency baseline (human vs machine vs derived)
edges.example: derived indexing makes consistency a vocabulary-coverage question
edges.resolution_rule: interpret consistency relative to chosen method

edges.why_related: target scheme defines the class label space for automation
edges.example: auto-classifier predicts into DDC/LCC class set
edges.resolution_rule: scheme label space dominates classifier design

edges.why_related: assigned index supplies training labels for automation
edges.example: manually assigned classes train the auto-classifier
edges.resolution_rule: secure label policy before training classifier

edges.why_related: taxonomy/vocabulary defines the multi-label target set
edges.example: tagger predicts into the controlled taxonomy
edges.resolution_rule: vocabulary defines categorization label set

edges.why_related: both automate subject assignment but differ in single vs multi-label and shelf vs topical
edges.example: shelf auto-classification vs multi-label topical tagging
edges.resolution_rule: keep distinct eval metrics; share feature pipeline

edges.why_related: hierarchy is built on the vocabulary's terms
edges.example: BT/NT chains link existing headings
edges.resolution_rule: define terms before hierarchical relations

edges.why_related: facet structure constrains how hierarchy and collocation are organized
edges.example: facet schedule sets collocation order within hierarchy
edges.resolution_rule: facets bound hierarchy/collocation order

edges.why_related: entry vocabulary maps user words to preferred controlled terms
edges.example: lead-in 'corn' routes to preferred 'maize'
edges.resolution_rule: entry vocabulary requires preferred terms first

edges.why_related: local vocabulary is the source side of crosswalks
edges.example: mapping local subjects to LCSH
edges.resolution_rule: stabilize vocabulary before crosswalking

edges.why_related: the chosen scheme is one endpoint of scheme crosswalks
edges.risk_of_conflict: mapping to undecided scheme is moot
edges.example: DDC<->LCC crosswalk needs both schemes fixed
edges.resolution_rule: fix scheme before mapping to others

edges.why_related: maintenance operates on the established vocabulary/authority file
edges.example: merging/retiring headings in the authority file
edges.resolution_rule: build vocabulary before maintenance lifecycle

edges.why_related: warrant policy guides which maintenance add/retire actions are justified
edges.example: retiring an unwarranted heading on review
edges.resolution_rule: apply warrant test to maintenance changes

edges.why_related: exhaustivity/specificity directly move precision and recall
edges.example: raising exhaustivity raises recall lowers precision
edges.resolution_rule: tune depth to hit precision/recall targets

edges.why_related: controlled/free mix changes precision/recall profile
edges.example: free-text raises recall but lowers precision
edges.resolution_rule: set mix to meet precision/recall design targets

edges.why_related: inconsistent indexing caps achievable retrieval precision/recall
edges.example: low consistency makes recall depend on which indexer worked
edges.resolution_rule: raise consistency before fine precision/recall tuning

edges.why_related: entry vocabulary breadth changes recall for user-worded queries
edges.example: adding lead-in synonyms raises novice-query recall
edges.resolution_rule: balance entry breadth against precision target

edges.why_related: precision/recall targets define what the harness must measure
edges.example: harness reports recall@k against design targets
edges.resolution_rule: design targets precede harness metric set

edges.why_related: consistency measurement is part of the evaluation harness
edges.example: harness computes Hooper consistency on dual-indexed sample
edges.resolution_rule: fold consistency into the harness

edges.why_related: classifier quality must be measured by the harness
edges.example: CI fails on macro-F1 drop after retraining
edges.resolution_rule: route classifier metrics through the harness

edges.why_related: governance decisions consume evaluation evidence
edges.example: board approves change only after harness regression passes
edges.resolution_rule: require eval evidence for governance sign-off

edges.why_related: governance review gates bound which maintenance changes may finalize
edges.example: scheme migration needs change-control approval
edges.resolution_rule: governance gates dominate maintenance finalization

edges.why_related: governance can trigger re-evaluation of scheme choice
edges.example: audit triggers reconsidering scheme after collection shift; stop once fit re-confirmed
edges.resolution_rule: revisit scheme only on material misfit; stop after re-confirmation

edges.why_related: controlled-quality indexing competes with cheap automated/derived scaling
edges.example: auto-derived tags scale but lose controlled precision
edges.resolution_rule: favor controlled assignment for high-stakes classes; automate the long tail

edges.why_related: raising exhaustivity for recall fights precision targets
edges.example: deep indexing for recall floods results lowering precision
edges.resolution_rule: resolve per query-class priority set in design targets

edges.why_related: faceted expressiveness fights notation simplicity/transcribability
edges.example: rich faceted strings raise transcription error rate
edges.resolution_rule: cap notation length; prefer expressiveness only where compoundness warrants

edges.why_related: responsive maintenance speed fights governance review overhead
edges.example: urgent term fix waits on board approval
edges.resolution_rule: fast-track low-risk edits; gate high-impact/irreversible ones

conflict_axes.trigger: large/streaming corpus needs scale but high-stakes access needs controlled precision
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: controlled assignment dominates high-stakes classes; automation dominates the long tail
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: auto-classification proposed for legally/medically high-stakes classes
conflict_axes.example: auto-routing medical subjects vs MeSH assignment

conflict_axes.trigger: raising exhaustivity for recall lowers precision and vice versa
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the query class with higher business value sets the depth target
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: precision and recall both fall below target for a key query class

conflict_axes.trigger: expressive faceted notation raises transcription complexity/error
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: simplicity dominates unless subject compoundness warrants expressiveness

conflict_axes.trigger: urgent vocabulary fixes conflict with review-gate overhead
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: governance dominates high-impact/irreversible changes; speed dominates low-risk edits
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: irreversible change requested under time pressure
conflict_axes.example: urgent term fix vs board approval

conflict_axes.trigger: controlled precision vs free-text novelty coverage
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: controlled dominates established concepts; free-text supplements for novelty
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: free-text noise or controlled miss-rate exceeds target

conflict_axes.trigger: consistent controlled assignment vs cheap scalable derivation
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: assignment dominates where concepts are not stated verbatim in text
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: derived method used for concepts absent from text
conflict_axes.example: extracting title keywords vs assigning MeSH

conflict_axes.trigger: local-fit scheme/vocabulary choices reduce crosswalk fidelity
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: interoperability dominates when federation is required; local fit dominates otherwise
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: federation mandate added after local scheme chosen
conflict_axes.example: local subjects map only broadly to LCSH

conflict_axes.trigger: high exhaustivity raises cost and lowers consistency
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: depth is capped at the level sustaining target consistency within budget
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: consistency drops or cost spikes as depth rises

conflict_axes.trigger: stable terms aid legacy access but lag emerging terminology
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: stability dominates for legacy access; add new terms only with warrant and migration
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: emerging-term gap rate high while legacy churn risk high
conflict_axes.example: new tech terms missing for years

edge_cases.trigger: a node references a non-existent dependency id
edge_cases.example: edge points to deleted node id
edge_cases.detection_method: reference integrity scan over node/edge ids

edge_cases.trigger: notation diverges from selected scheme conventions
edge_cases.example: custom codes inserted into a DDC adoption
edge_cases.detection_method: conformance check of notation against scheme rules
resolution: realign notation to scheme or document custom deviation

edge_cases.trigger: automated metrics presented as observed without data
edge_cases.detection_method: label audit: no observed labels without observed dataset

edge_cases.trigger: a single node bundles vocabulary build + maintenance + mapping
edge_cases.example: one node covers thesaurus build and crosswalking
edge_cases.detection_method: node scope review against grain rule

edge_cases.example: scheme selection finalized without coverage test
freezing classmarks before scheme review passes

edge_cases.trigger: governance feedback loops without stop condition
edge_cases.example: scheme re-selected repeatedly on minor signals
edge_cases.detection_method: loop detection on feedback edges + iteration counts

edge_cases.trigger: a tradeoff modeled as a dependency
edge_cases.detection_method: edge-type audit separating conflict from dependency
resolution: split into separate conflict + dependency edges

edge_cases.trigger: dependent node ordered before its prerequisite
edge_cases.detection_method: topological check of priority_order vs dependencies
freshness check on warrant evidence dates

edge_cases.trigger: workflow step omits required handoff artifact
edge_cases.example: eval step hands off without regression baseline
edge_cases.detection_method: handoff artifact completeness check per step

edge_cases.trigger: computed score inconsistent with its formula
edge_cases.detection_method: recompute all derived scores and diff within tolerance

workflow.objective: fix scope, unit of analysis, users, and exclusions
acceptance_tests: every later node maps to an in-scope unit
workflow.do_first_because: scope is the highest-coupling foundation all later choices depend on

workflow.objective: select scheme, paradigm, facets, and notation
workflow.do_first_because: scheme/paradigm/notation are high-irreversibility foundations for all classification

workflow.objective: build controlled vocabulary, warrant, hierarchy, and entry vocabulary
acceptance_tests: sampled synonyms map to one preferred term
sampled terms place under correct BT/NT
workflow.do_first_because: vocabulary is a high-coupling foundation for indexing policy, automation, and access

workflow.objective: set controlled/free mix, exhaustivity/specificity, and assignment vs derivation
workflow.do_first_because: policy depends on vocabulary and frames every downstream indexing and automation choice

workflow.objective: design automated classification and multi-label categorization with fallback
acceptance_tests: macro-F1 meets target per class group
low-confidence items routed to human review
workflow.do_first_because: automation depends on scheme label space and assigned training labels

workflow.objective: finalize browsing access and external crosswalks
acceptance_tests: sampled mappings carry correct match type
workflow.do_first_because: access and crosswalks depend on a stable vocabulary

workflow.objective: measure consistency, precision/recall, classifier quality and set regression baseline
workflow.do_first_because: evaluation must precede any hard lock or governance sign-off

workflow.objective: establish vocabulary/scheme maintenance lifecycle and reindexing
acceptance_tests: sampled changed terms propagate to existing records
workflow.do_first_because: maintenance can only run once vocabulary and evaluation exist

workflow.objective: stand up governance: policy of record, decision log, review gates
acceptance_tests: high-impact decisions carry decision records + sign-off
workflow.do_first_because: governance consumes evaluation evidence and gates irreversible changes

workflow.objective: validate, hard-lock approved artifacts, and hand off the system
acceptance_tests: validator passes with no hard failures
workflow.do_first_because: hard lock is only permitted after dependency, validation, and human-review gates pass

notation is costly to change later

connects user words to preferred terms
gates irreversible decisions, depends on eval

priority_rationale.notes: unlocks facet analysis and notation synthesis
notation is costly to change later
unlocks policy, hierarchy, access, automation, maintenance
connects user words to preferred terms
gates irreversible decisions, depends on eval

dominance_rules.rule: risk control dominates delivery speed for risk_if_wrong>=0.80 nodes
dominance_rules.required_action: run acceptance tests and human review before finalizing
dominance_rules.example: do not finalize scheme migration fast without coverage tests

dominance_rules.trigger: dependency precedence conflicts with value ordering
dominance_rules.rule: dependency order dominates raw value ordering in priority
dominance_rules.example: build vocabulary before indexing-policy even if policy seems higher value
report estimated F1 as heuristic not observed

dominance_rules.trigger: artifact proposed for lock before QA passes
dominance_rules.required_action: pass acceptance/regression gates before any lock
dominance_rules.example: do not hard-lock notation before scheme review passes

dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation for irreversible or low-confidence cases
dominance_rules.required_action: route low-confidence/irreversible items to human review
dominance_rules.example: low-confidence auto-classifications go to a cataloger

dominance_rules.trigger: pressure to add nodes/edges threatens schema stability
dominance_rules.example: freeze node structure before padding edges

dominance_rules.trigger: tradeoff between JSON validity and richer prose
dominance_rules.required_action: ensure strict JSON first, trim prose if needed
dominance_rules.example: shorten examples rather than break JSON

dominance_rules.required_action: attach evidence_refs or downgrade/remove the claim
dominance_rules.example: warrant claims must cite warrant evidence

dominance_rules.trigger: output budget threatened by excessive density
dominance_rules.required_action: reduce weak similarity edges and examples before required content
dominance_rules.example: drop a similarity edge before dropping a required dependency

dominance_rules.required_action: sequence foundations first even if a later step looks ready

dominance_rules.trigger: a score uses an undefined or hidden variable
dominance_rules.rule: explicit formula inputs dominate hidden assumptions
dominance_rules.required_action: store every formula variable in node/edge/score_derivation_inputs

dominance_rules.trigger: a convenient sequencing introduces a dependency cycle
dominance_rules.required_action: convert the weaker dependency to sequence/feedback
dominance_rules.example: governance->scheme is feedback, not a dependency cycle

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not finalize scheme before scope is locked
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: scheme chosen while scope still in draft
anti_rework_rules.example: selecting LCC before excluding full-text scope

anti_rework_rules.rule: draft competency questions before populating nodes
anti_rework_rules.rationale: untargeted nodes get rebuilt to answer missed questions
anti_rework_rules.example: building nodes before knowing what to answer

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not finalize indexing policy before vocabulary exists
anti_rework_rules.rationale: policy assumptions invalid without a vocabulary
